_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every value the Android app and the offline eval
harness (tools/eval_clustering.py) must agree on. The harness replays real
captured windows through the same pipeline to evaluate prompt/model changes —
the moment it diverges from shipped code it stops predicting the app's
behaviour, which is exactly the failure this file prevents.
Kotlin reads it at BUILD time: a Gradle task generates SharedConfig.kt from it
(see app/build.gradle.kts), so these stay compile-time constants with no runtime
parsing on the digest path. Python reads it directly at run time.
Change a value here and BOTH sides pick it up on their next run. Never copy a
value out of here into either language.
App-internal constants with no cross-language counterpart (HTTP retry counts,
timeouts, heartbeat intervals, notification channel ids) deliberately stay in
their own Kotlin companion objects — putting them here would add build coupling
